Proposition
[Curvature equations for distance functions]

Source: petersen:page-0115, petersen:page-0116 ↗ cor:pet-ch3-radial-equation-distance-function ↗ thm:pet-ch3-radial-curvature-equation

1. ch3:3.2.11For a distance function $r:(O,g) o \mathbb R$ with $\partial _r= abla r$:

  1. $\mathcal L_{\partial _r}g=2\operatorname {Hess}r$;

  2. $( abla _{\partial _r}\operatorname {Hess}r)(X,Y)+\operatorname {Hess}^2r(X,Y)=-R(X,\partial _r,\partial _r,Y)$;

  3. $(\mathcal L_{\partial _r}\operatorname {Hess}r)(X,Y)-\operatorname {Hess}^2r(X,Y)=-R(X,\partial _r,\partial _r,Y)$.

Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch3-distance-function-curvature-equations

\sketch The identity $\mathcal L_{ abla f}g=2\operatorname {Hess}f$ gives (1). Apply the two $(0,2)$ radial curvature equations to $f=r$; since $| abla r|=1$, $\operatorname {Hess}( frac 12| abla r|^2)=0$, yielding (2) and (3).

□
